steps.tx: **Guillain-Barré syndrome** (GBS) classically manifests as an acute, ascending, symmetrical flaccid **quadriparesis** with generalized hyporeflexia or areflexia, reaching nadir within 4 weeks. Symptoms typically follow a gastrointestinal or respiratory illness, with Campylobacter jejuni being the most frequent antecedent pathogen provoking molecular mimicry.
steps.say: Guillain Barré syndrome is an acute post infectious polyradiculoneuropathy characterized by rapidly progressive symmetrical ascending flaccid weakness and areflexia. Symptoms typically develop within two to four weeks of a gastrointestinal or respiratory illness. Campylobacter jejuni infection serves as the most frequent antecedent trigger through ganglioside molecular mimicry.

steps.tx: **Charcot-Marie-Tooth** disease type 1A (CMT1A) is the most common hereditary neuropathy, caused by a **1.4** Mb duplication of the **PMP22** gene on chromosome 17p11.2, resulting in uniform nerve conduction slowing. This contrasts with acute motor axonal neuropathy (AMAN), which features anti-GD1a antibodies and rapid axolemmal injury.
steps.say: Charcot Marie Tooth disease type one A is the most common hereditary neuropathy, caused by duplication of the PMP22 gene on chromosome seventeen. This contrasts with acute motor axonal neuropathy, an acquired variant of Guillain Barré syndrome linked to anti ganglioside antibodies.

steps.tx: The Miller Fisher syndrome is a distinct cranial variant of Guillain-Barré syndrome presenting with a classic clinical triad: **ophthalmoplegia**, **ataxia**, and **areflexia**, typically sparing limb motor power. Over 90% of patients with Miller Fisher syndrome demonstrate high titers of serum antibodies against the **GQ1b** ganglioside, which is enriched in the paranodal myelin of the oculomotor, trochlear, abducens, and primary sensory afferent nerves.
steps.say: Miller Fisher syndrome is a recognized cranial variant of Guillain Barré syndrome presenting with ophthalmoplegia, sensory ataxia, and generalized areflexia. Over ninety percent of affected patients test positive for circulating anti GQ1b IgG antibodies. The GQ1b ganglioside is densely expressed within ocular motor nerves and muscle spindle afferents.

rows: Areflexia with limb power often spared

steps.tx: **Albuminocytological dissociation** in **CSF**, defined as elevated protein with normal total leukocyte count (<50 cells/uL, typically <5 cells/uL), is typical in GBS, though CSF protein may be normal within the first week of symptoms. Protein levels rise progressively during subsequent weeks, peaking at two to three weeks.
steps.say: Lumbar puncture in Guillain Barré syndrome classically reveals albuminocytological dissociation, with elevated protein alongside a normal white blood cell count under five cells per microliter. Cerebrospinal fluid protein levels can remain normal during the first week of symptoms, characteristically rising to peak levels during the second and third weeks.

rows: Normal protein does not rule out acute GBS
Consider HIV, Lyme disease, or sarcoidosis

steps.tx: First-line disease-modifying immunotherapies for Guillain-Barré syndrome are intravenous **immunoglobulin** (IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days) or **plasma exchange** (PLEX), which have proven equal clinical efficacy. Combining both immunotherapeutic modalities confers no additive benefit and significantly increases healthcare costs without accelerating functional recovery.
steps.say: Intravenous immunoglobulin administered at zero point four grams per kilogram daily for five days and therapeutic plasma exchange demonstrate equivalent clinical efficacy. Treatment should begin promptly in patients unable to walk unaided or with progressive autonomic or respiratory compromise. Combining both treatments confers no additive benefit, and systemic corticosteroids are ineffective.

steps.tx: Systemic **corticosteroids** administered alone are ineffective in **Guillain-Barré** syndrome and are not recommended for acute therapy. Bedside spirometry monitoring forced vital capacity is essential to guide elective endotracheal intubation when forced vital capacity falls below 20 mL/kg or negative inspiratory pressure weakens.
steps.say: Respiratory muscle paralysis is the most critical life threatening emergency in Guillain Barré syndrome. Clinicians must perform bedside spirometric monitoring of forced vital capacity every four to six hours. The twenty thirty forty rule provides a practical guide for elective intubation before acute respiratory arrest occurs.

steps.tx: Chronic **inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy** (**CIDP**) is distinguished from acute Guillain-Barré syndrome by progressive or relapsing sensory and motor deficits continuing beyond 8 weeks, responding favourably to maintenance IVIG, plasma exchange, or oral corticosteroids. Corticosteroid responsiveness represents a fundamental clinical difference from acute post-infectious GBS.
steps.say: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy presents with progressive or relapsing symmetrical weakness and sensory loss evolving over at least eight weeks. Unlike acute Guillain Barré syndrome, CIDP improves with systemic corticosteroid therapy as well as regular intravenous immunoglobulin infusions or plasma exchange.

left.title: Guillain-Barre syndrome
points: IVIG or plasma exchange first line

steps.tx: **Multifocal motor neuropathy** (MMN) presents with asymmetric progressive distal upper limb motor weakness without sensory involvement, demonstrating persistent motor conduction block and high titers of **anti-GM1** IgM antibodies in over 50% of cases, responding selectively to IVIG while worsening with corticosteroid treatment.
steps.say: Multifocal motor neuropathy presents as an asymmetric, purely motor neuropathy characterized by upper limb weakness without sensory loss, mimicking lower motor neuron disease. Nerve conduction studies establish the diagnosis by demonstrating focal motor conduction block in non entrapment segments. High titers of anti GM1 IgM antibodies occur in over half of cases, and intravenous immunoglobulin represents the treatment of choice.
